The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the referenced cotangent and symplectic-action conventions. Work on affine Minkowski spacetime with inertial coordinates $x^0=ct,x^1,x^2,x^3$ in metres, metric matrix $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and cotangent coordinates $(x^a,p_a)$, where each $p_a$ has SI momentum units. Fix the future cone as the timelike component containing the positive $x^0$ axis, equivalently $v^0>\lvert\mathbf v\rvert$. Let $SO^+(1,3)$ denote the determinant-one, future-cone-preserving Lorentz subgroup. Define the proper orthochronous Poincaré group and its multiplication by

$$G=\mathbb R^4\rtimes SO^+(1,3),\qquad (a,\Lambda)(b,L)=(a+\Lambda b,\Lambda L).$$

Its action on spacetime and the cotangent lift are $x'=\Lambda x+a$ and $p'=\Lambda^{-T}p$. The Lie algebra consists of pairs $(a,A)$ with $A^T\eta+\eta A=0$, bracket

$$[(a,A),(b,B)]=(Ab-Ba,[A,B]).$$

Use the library convention $\xi_M=\left.\frac d{ds}\right|_0\exp_G(-s\xi)\cdot z$. Thus the positive affine generator on spacetime is $Y_{(a,A)}(x)=a+Ax$, the fundamental field is its negative, and the cotangent-lifted positive field is $(a+Ax,-A^Tp)$. Pair the cotangent point with a Lie-algebra element by

$$\ell_{(a,A)}(x,p)=p_b(a^b+A^b{}_cx^c).$$

Define $P^a=\eta^{ab}p_b$ and $J^{ab}=x^aP^b-x^bP^a$. The equivalent dual pairing is $\ell_{(a,A)}=p_ba^b-\tfrac12J_{bc}A^{bc}$, where $A^{bc}=A^b{}_d\eta^{dc}$ and $J_{bc}=\eta_{bd}\eta_{ce}J^{de}$. Here $[P^a]=\mathrm{kg\,m/s}$ and $[J^{ab}]=\mathrm{J\,s}$. These are charge-space definitions on the full cotangent bundle; shell reduction and the moment-map identities are stated separately. No spin or particle model is included.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For the group and cotangent conventions of [[def-rpm-h-poincare-charge-space]], the map $\mu:T^*\mathbb R^4\to\mathfrak g^*$ defined by $\langle\mu(x,p),(a,A)\rangle=\ell_{(a,A)}(x,p)$ is a smooth equivariant moment map and obeys

$$\{\ell_\xi,\ell_\eta\}=\ell_{[\xi,\eta]},\quad \{P^a,P^b\}=0,\quad \{J^{ab},P^c\}=\eta^{ac}P^b-\eta^{bc}P^a,$$

$$\{J^{ab},J^{cd}\}=\eta^{ac}J^{bd}-\eta^{ad}J^{bc}-\eta^{bc}J^{ad}+\eta^{bd}J^{ac}.$$

For shell coordinates write $\mathbf p=(p_1,p_2,p_3)$ and $|\mathbf p|^2:=p_1^2+p_2^2+p_3^2$. For each future massive shell with $m>0$ in kg, $c>0$ in m/s, $p_0=-E/c$, and $E=\sqrt{m^2c^4+c^2|\mathbf p|^2}$, or nonzero future null shell with $m=0$ and $|\mathbf p|>0$, its Poincare charges descend to the global ray quotient. For vectors $u,v\in\mathbb R^4$, define $(u\wedge v)^{ab}:=u^av^b-u^bv^a$. The induced dual action is $(P,J)\mapsto(\Lambda P,\Lambda J\Lambda^T+a\wedge\Lambda P)$. On the fixed-time slice $x^0=ct$, with physical position $q^i=x^i$, the boost component $B_i=J^{0i}=ct p_i-q^iE/c$ is explicitly time dependent and satisfies $\partial_tB_i+\{B_i,E\}=0$. These are mathematical identities; conservation is conditional on the stated free-shell evolution.

In affine Minkowski space with inertial coordinates $x^0,x^i$ measured in metres and metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, let $m\ge0$ and let

$$\Sigma_m^+=\{(x,p): -p_0=P^0=\sqrt{m^2c^2+|\mathbf p|^2},\ p_0<0\},$$

where $\mathbf p\ne0$ when $m=0$, and write $P^i=p_i$ for the spatial raised momentum components. The characteristic flow of the restricted canonical form is $(x,p)\mapsto(x+\alpha P,p)$, and its orbit space is globally diffeomorphic to $B_m=\mathbb R^3_a\times\mathbb R^3_p$ for $m>0$, or $\mathbb R^3_a\times(\mathbb R^3_p\setminus\{0\})$ for $m=0$, by

$$a^i=x^i-\frac{P^i}{P^0}x^0,\qquad p_i=p_i.$$

The reduced symplectic form is $da^i\wedge dp_i$. The quotient is Hausdorff and second countable and each full characteristic line meets each slice $x^0=ct$ exactly once. This is an explicit free flat quotient, not a conclusion about arbitrary first-class systems.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $\mathcal O\subseteq\mathfrak g^*$ be a
coadjoint orbit with its canonical immersed homogeneous-space structure and let
$\omega$ be the KKS form of
[[def-kirillov-kostant-souriau-form-on-a-coadjoint-orbit]]. Then $\omega$ is a
smooth, closed, nondegenerate two-form on $\mathcal O$, so $(\mathcal O,\omega)$
is a symplectic manifold. It is $G$-invariant, and the inclusion
$\Phi:\mathcal O\hookrightarrow\mathfrak g^*$ satisfies the component moment
equations $d\langle\Phi,\xi\rangle=-\iota_{\xi_{\mathcal O}}\omega$ for the
coadjoint action. It is the unique two-form on $\mathcal O$ for which the
inclusion is an infinitesimal moment map, hence in particular the unique
$G$-invariant symplectic form with that property.

derivations.claim: In a rest frame $P=(mc,0)$, $W=0$ is equivalent to $J^{ij}=0$, since its three spatial components are an invertible multiple of the three spatial angular-momentum components. The remaining $J^{0i}$ are produced explicitly by $x^0=0$, $x^i=-J^{0i}/(mc)$, since $J=x\wedge P$ then has exactly those components and $J^{ij}=0$. Lorentz transforming this representative gives a position representative for every future timelike $P$ with $W=0$. Equivalently for a transverse representative $x\cdot P=0$, $x^a=J^{ab}P_b/P^2$, as substitution of $J=x\wedge P$ gives $J^{ab}P_b=x^aP^2-(x\cdot P)P^a$. This characterization is Lorentz covariant.

H8's quotient point $(a,p)$ maps to $P^0=E/c$, $P^i=p_i$, $J^{0i}=-a^iP^0$, and $J^{ij}=a^ip_j-a^jp_i$. The inverse is $p_i=P^i$, $a^i=-J^{0i}/P^0$, smooth since $P^0>0$. These mutually inverse smooth coordinates make the image an embedded six-dimensional graph and show the quotient map is a diffeomorphism onto the charge locus of step 1.1.

A proper orthochronous boost sends each future massive $P$ to rest. By step 1.1 its $W=0$ charge then has only $J^{0i}$ components, and a translation removes those components. Thus every pair in the locus is in the orbit of $(mc,0;0)$; conversely $P^2$ and $W=0$ are invariant under the coadjoint action. The stabilizer at rest consists of spatial rotations and translations parallel to $P$, dimension $3+1=4$, so the orbit dimension is $10-4=6$. The six smooth orbit coordinates $p_i=P^i$, $a^i=-J^{0i}/P^0$ from step 2.1 have injective differential: if their differentials vanish, the graph formulas in step 2.1 make every component of $(P,J)$ have zero differential, and the coadjoint-orbit inclusion is an immersion. Since both manifolds have dimension six, the inverse function theorem makes this coordinate map a local diffeomorphism. The bijection in step 2.1 is therefore a global diffeomorphism for the canonical orbit smooth structure.

Let $\rho:\Sigma_m^+\to B_m$ be the H8 quotient and $\iota:\Sigma_m^+\hookrightarrow T^*\mathbb R^4$ the inclusion. H8 states $\rho^*\omega_{\rm red}=\iota^*\omega$. The cotangent action of $g=(a,\Lambda)$ preserves this future shell: $P'=\Lambda P$ preserves its norm and future cone, and it maps the full characteristic line $(x+\alpha P,p)$ to $(\Lambda x+a+\alpha\Lambda P,\Lambda^{-T}p)$, which is exactly a characteristic line with momentum $P'$. The inverse group element gives the converse. Therefore the quotient action is well-defined. It is smooth because the global section $\sigma(a^i,p_i)$ given by $x^0=0$, $x^i=a^i$ is smooth and $g\cdot b=\rho(g\cdot\sigma(b))$ is its explicit expression; fibre preservation gives the group law independently of the chosen section. The cotangent action is symplectic by [L1], so pulling back along the surjective submersion $\rho$ gives $\rho^*(g^*\omega_{\rm red})=g^*\iota^*\omega=\iota^*\omega=\rho^*\omega_{\rm red}$, hence the quotient action preserves $\omega_{\rm red}$. Differentiating $\rho(\exp(-s\xi)\cdot z)=\exp(-s\xi)\cdot\rho(z)$ at $s=0$ gives $d\rho(\xi_{\Sigma_m^+})=\xi_{B_m}$ with the library's same fundamental-field convention. The moment components from [L1] are constant on each characteristic fibre since $P$ is fixed and $(x+\alpha P)\wedge P=x\wedge P$. Thus for any tangent $v$ on $B_m$ choose a lift $\tilde v$ and obtain $d\bar\mu^\xi(v)=d\mu^\xi(\tilde v)=-\omega_{\rm red}(\xi_{B_m},v)$. On the orbit [F2] gives the same moment equation. Its fundamental fields span each tangent space, so these equations determine both two-forms pointwise and show the diffeomorphism in step 3.1 pulls KKS back to $\omega_{\rm red}=da^i\wedge dp_i$.

Assume countable choice ACω, as in [[def-countable-choice]], for the smooth cotangent-bundle carrier convention used by this page; no full Axiom of Choice is assumed.

Let $\mathcal D$ be an open subset of the time-dependent tangent bundle $\mathbb R\times TQ$ of a finite-dimensional smooth manifold $Q$, and let $L:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R$ be smooth. For fixed $t$, the **fibre derivative** is the map

$$\mathbb F L(t,q,v)=(t,q,p),\qquad p(w)=\left.\frac{d}{ds}\right|_{s=0}L(t,q,v+sw),$$

as in [[def-fibre-derivative-and-legendre-transform-of-a-lagrangian]]. In induced coordinates $p_i=\partial L/\partial v^i$.

The Lagrangian is **regular** at $(t,q,v)$ when the velocity Hessian $(\partial^2L/\partial v^i\partial v^j)$ is invertible there; regularity gives only a local inverse branch. It is **hyperregular on a declared domain** when $\mathbb F L$ is a diffeomorphism from that entire domain onto an open subset of $\mathbb R\times T^*Q$.

It is **almost regular on a declared domain $\mathcal D_0\subseteq\mathcal D$** when the following are all assumed: $\mathbb F L|_{\mathcal D_0}$ has constant rank; its image $N$ is an embedded submanifold of $\mathbb R\times T^*Q$; its corestriction $\mathcal D_0\to N$ is a surjective submersion (its differential is surjective at every point); and every fibre of that corestriction is connected. These hypotheses are not consequences of singularity alone.

A mathematical **observable** on this phase space means a smooth function $F:T^*Q\to\mathbb R$; this definition does not assert that a measurement has been performed or that every such function is physically measurable.

For an interpreted particle model, assign coordinates $q^i$ their declared units and assign the conjugate covector components $p_i$ units of action divided by the units of $q^i$. Thus $\theta$ and $\omega$ have action units, conventionally joule-seconds, and a bracket of quantities with units \([F]\) and \([G]\) has units \([F][G]/(\text{action})\). $$C:=\{z\in U:\chi_1(z)=\cdots=\chi_r(z)=0\}$$

when $d\chi_1(z),\ldots,d\chi_r(z)$ are linearly independent at every $z\in C$. The regular-level theorem [[thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold]] then gives $C$ its embedded-submanifold structure and $T_zC=\bigcap_a\ker d\chi_a(z)$. $$H_T(t,z):=H_c(t,z)+\sum_{a=1}^r u^a(t)\chi_a(z).$$

The functions $u^a$ are independent parameter functions; the definition does not assert that their equations determine them. If $H_c$ is an energy and $\chi_a$ has units \([\chi_a]\), then $u^a$ has units energy divided by \([\chi_a]\), so every term in $H_T$ has the same units. A later constraint, if generated by consistency, is not declared primary by this definition.

Use the signature $(-,+,+,+)$ throughout. In the flat case, **Minkowski spacetime** means the affine model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]: $A$ is an affine space, $\eta$ is a nondegenerate Lorentz form on its four-dimensional displacement space, and $C^+$ selects the future cone. In the curved case, a **background spacetime** means a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]; the metric and time orientation are fixed data, not dynamical unknowns here. No field equation or completeness assumption is included.

A **massive worldline** on an open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a $C^2$ curve $x:I\to M$ with future-directed timelike tangent $T=dx/ds$ at every parameter value. This is the smooth subclass of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. A **null worldline** is a $C^2$ curve with nonzero future-directed null tangent everywhere. Its tangent has no proper-time normalization: $g(T,T)=0$, so the massive proper-time formula does not apply. An **observer at an event** $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Its instantaneous rest space is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$. This is a pointwise vector-space construction; the definition does not assign a clock reading or a moving frame to a lone observer.

An **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth field of future unit timelike vectors on $U$, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]; its observer curves are its integral curves. A **tetrad** is a chosen orthonormal frame field, as in [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. A **chart** is a coordinate map; an adapted chart is a chart whose spatial coordinates are constant along the congruence's integral curves. These objects are distinct: a chart need not be inertial, a tetrad need not be coordinate induced, and a congruence is a field of observers rather than a chart or a frame. This distinction agrees with [[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]].

The coordinates and units used later are SI: in an inertial chart $x^0=ct$ and $x^i$ are metres, $t$ is seconds, $c>0$ is metres per second, and proper time is measured in seconds. In a general chart, coordinate components inherit their coordinate units; invariant equations are tensorial. No global inertial chart, global tetrad, or global observer congruence is asserted to exist.

It is **almost regular on a declared domain $\mathcal D_0\subseteq\mathcal D$** when the following are all assumed: $\mathbb F L|_{\mathcal D_0}$ has constant rank; its image $N$ is an embedded submanifold of $\mathbb R\times T^*Q$; its corestriction $\mathcal D_0\to N$ is a surjective submersion (its differential is surjective at every point); and every fibre of that corestriction is connected. These hypotheses are not consequences of singularity alone.

Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$: every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary, of dimension $n$. Its cotangent bundle is

$$T^*Q=\coprod_{q\in Q}T_q^*Q,\qquad \pi:T^*Q\to Q,\quad \pi(q,p)=q,$$

with the canonical smooth structure and induced cotangent charts supplied by the manifold construction in [[def-tautological-one-form-on-a-cotangent-bundle]]. The **tautological one-form** is $\theta_{(q,p)}(\xi)=p(d\pi_{(q,p)}\xi)$, and the **canonical cotangent two-form** is $\omega=-d\theta$. The exact theorem [[thm-the-canonical-cotangent-two-form-is-symplectic]] makes $(T^*Q,\omega)$ a symplectic manifold in the sense of [[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]]. We call this pair the **cotangent phase space** of $Q$.

In an induced chart $(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$, $\theta=p_i\,dq^i$ and $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$. A mathematical **observable** on this phase space means a smooth function $F:T^*Q\to\mathbb R$; this definition does not assert that a measurement has been performed or that every such function is physically measurable.

For an interpreted particle model, assign coordinates $q^i$ their declared units and assign the conjugate covector components $p_i$ units of action divided by the units of $q^i$. Thus $\theta$ and $\omega$ have action units, conventionally joule-seconds, and a bracket of quantities with units \([F]\) and \([G]\) has units \([F][G]/(\text{action})\). These are dimensional interpretations of the model, not additional mathematical premises. The use of $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ is exactly the use in the smooth cotangent-bundle suppliers; no full Axiom of Choice is used.

$$C:=\{z\in U:\chi_1(z)=\cdots=\chi_r(z)=0\}$$

when $d\chi_1(z),\ldots,d\chi_r(z)$ are linearly independent at every $z\in C$. The regular-level theorem [[thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold]] then gives $C$ its embedded-submanifold structure and $T_zC=\bigcap_a\ker d\chi_a(z)$. For functions $F,G$ on $U$, write $F\approx G$ when $F|_C=G|_C$; thus $F\approx0$ means that $F$ vanishes on $C$, without requiring it to vanish off $C$.

Given a smooth canonical Hamiltonian $H_c$ on $U$ and multiplier functions $u^a(t)$, the **total generator** is

$$H_T(t,z):=H_c(t,z)+\sum_{a=1}^r u^a(t)\chi_a(z).$$

The functions $u^a$ are independent parameter functions; the definition does not assert that their equations determine them. If $H_c$ is an energy and $\chi_a$ has units \([\chi_a]\), then $u^a$ has units energy divided by \([\chi_a]\), so every term in $H_T$ has the same units. A later constraint, if generated by consistency, is not declared primary by this definition.

Use the signature $(-,+,+,+)$ throughout. In the flat case, **Minkowski spacetime** means the affine model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]: $A$ is an affine space, $\eta$ is a nondegenerate Lorentz form on its four-dimensional displacement space, and $C^+$ selects the future cone. In the curved case, a **background spacetime** means a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]; the metric and time orientation are fixed data, not dynamical unknowns here. No field equation or completeness assumption is included.

A **massive worldline** on an open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a $C^2$ curve $x:I\to M$ with future-directed timelike tangent $T=dx/ds$ at every parameter value. This is the smooth subclass of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. A **null worldline** is a $C^2$ curve with nonzero future-directed null tangent everywhere. Its tangent has no proper-time normalization: $g(T,T)=0$, so the massive proper-time formula does not apply. In the flat model these are affine curves into $A$ with tangent in the selected future timelike or null cone from [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]].

An **observer at an event** $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Its instantaneous rest space is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$. This is a pointwise vector-space construction; the definition does not assign a clock reading or a moving frame to a lone observer.

An **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth field of future unit timelike vectors on $U$, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]; its observer curves are its integral curves. A **tetrad** is a chosen orthonormal frame field, as in [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. A **chart** is a coordinate map; an adapted chart is a chart whose spatial coordinates are constant along the congruence's integral curves. These objects are distinct: a chart need not be inertial, a tetrad need not be coordinate induced, and a congruence is a field of observers rather than a chart or a frame. This distinction agrees with [[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]].

The coordinates and units used later are SI: in an inertial chart $x^0=ct$ and $x^i$ are metres, $t$ is seconds, $c>0$ is metres per second, and proper time is measured in seconds. In a general chart, coordinate components inherit their coordinate units; invariant equations are tensorial. No global inertial chart, global tetrad, or global observer congruence is asserted to exist.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $H\in C^\infty(U,\mathbb R)$ on an open set $U\subset\mathbb R\times T^*\mathbb R^n$, with coordinates $(t,q,p)$, and let $S_0\in C^\infty(Q_0,\mathbb R)$ on an open $Q_0\subset\mathbb R^n$. The Hamilton characteristic ODE is $\dot q^i=\partial H/\partial p_i$ and $\dot p_i=-\partial H/\partial q^i$. For a covector $p$ and vector $v$ in the canonical coordinates, write $p\cdot v:=\sum_i p_i v^i$. For each $a_0\in Q_0$ such that $(0,a_0,dS_0(a_0))\in U$, there are neighbourhoods of $(0,a_0)$ and a time interval on which this ODE with $q(0,a)=a$, $p(0,a)=dS_0(a)$ has a smooth solution and $(t,a)\mapsto(t,q(t,a))$ is a diffeomorphism onto its image after restriction. On that image the function

$$S(t,q(t,a))=S_0(a)+\int_0^t[p(u,a)\cdot\dot q(u,a)-H(u,q(u,a),p(u,a))],du$$

is smooth, has initial value $S_0$, and satisfies $S_t+H(t,q,S_q)=0$. The claim is local to the invertible projection domain; it asserts no continuation after a caustic. $S$ has action units, so $[S]=\mathrm{J\,s}$, $[S_q]=[p]$, and $[S_t]=\mathrm J$ when $t,q,p,H$ use SI time, length, momentum, and energy units.

Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $f:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be
$C^1$, and let $a\in U$.  If $Df(a)$ is invertible, then there are open sets
$V,W\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ with $a\in V\subseteq U$ and $f(a)\in W$ such that
$f|_V:V\to W$ is bijective.  Its inverse $g:W\to V$ is $C^1$, and

$$Dg(y)=Df(g(y))^{-1}\qquad(y\in W).$$

Thus $f$ is a local diffeomorphism at $a$.

Let $m\ge0$ and $c>0$. Assume a temporal product chart with lapse-shift data $(N,\beta,h)$ as in [[def-rpm-h-temporal-chart-data]], all four coordinates measured in metres. On the future shell $C_m=\tfrac12(g^{ab}p_ap_b+m^2c^2)=0$, define

$$\kappa=\sqrt{m^2c^2+h^{ij}p_ip_j},\quad p_0=\beta^ip_i-N\kappa,\quad H(t,q,p)=-cp_0=c(N\kappa-\beta^ip_i).$$

For $m=0$, require $p_i\ne0$. Let $J=[t_1,t_2]$ satisfy $t_1<t_2$ and $[ct_1,ct_2]\subset I$, where $I$ is the first-coordinate interval of the temporal product chart; require the path $t\mapsto(ct,q(t))$ to stay in the chart. The construction is local to this chart and intervals transverse to its time slices; no global curved-space gauge or quotient is asserted.

Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $c \in A$ be a limit point of $A$
([[def-limit-point-r]]), let $f, g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable at $c$
([[def-derivative]]) and let $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$. Then:

1. $f + g$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(f+g)'(c) = f'(c) + g'(c)$;
2. $\alpha f$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(\alpha f)'(c) = \alpha f'(c)$;
3. $fg$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(fg)'(c) = f'(c)g(c) + f(c)g'(c)$;
4. if $g(c) \ne 0$ then, writing $A_0 := \{\, x \in A : g(x) \ne 0 \,\}$, the
   point $c$ lies in $A_0$ and is a limit point of $A_0$, the quotient
   $(f/g)|_{A_0} : A_0 \to \mathbb{R}$, $x \mapsto f(x)/g(x)$, is differentiable
   at $c$ as a function on $A_0$, and
   $$\bigl((f/g)|_{A_0}\bigr)'(c) \;=\; \frac{f'(c)\,g(c) - f(c)\,g'(c)}{g(c)^{2}} .$$

Each claim asserts two things: that the derivative on the left exists, and that
it has the stated value. Both are proved.

**Why claim 4 is stated on $A_0$.** The function $f/g$ is not defined where $g$
vanishes, and $g$ may vanish at points of $A$ far from $c$; restricting to $A_0$
is forced. That the restriction still has $c$ as a limit point, so that a
derivative there means anything at all, is not free either, and it is the last
claim of [[lem-sign-preservation-near-a-limit]] applied to $g$. The hypothesis
is $g(c) \ne 0$, not "$g$ vanishes nowhere".

**Everything is proved through
[[thm-caratheodory-characterisation]].** No difference quotient is estimated and
no limit theorem beyond continuity is used, so no choice principle is spent.
The four identities are four algebraic rearrangements of an increment, each
followed by a reading of [[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]].

Let $f:U\to V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be totally differentiable at $a\in U$ and let $g:V\to\mathbb R^p$ be totally differentiable at $f(a)$. Then $g\circ f$ is totally differentiable at $a$ and

$$D(g\circ f)(a)=Dg(f(a))\circ Df(a).$$

The entries of $Df\circ g$ are $C^1$ by the chain rule. Matrix inversion on invertible matrices is $C^1$ entrywise by the cofactor-over-determinant formula, whose denominator is nonzero; finite products and reciprocal differentiation use the derivative algebra in [F1]. Consequently $Dg$ is $C^1$, and $g$ is $C^2$. At fixed $t$, the map $(q,\alpha)\mapsto(q,p=S_q)$ has derivative $\begin{pmatrix}I&0\\S_{qq}&S_{q\alpha}\end{pmatrix}$, which is invertible at the stated point. By [F1], after restriction it is a diffeomorphism and solves locally for $\alpha=\alpha(t,q,p)$. Keeping $t$ as an additional identity coordinate in $(t,q,\alpha)\mapsto(t,q,S_q)$ gives the same invertible block derivative and shows that the inverse $\alpha(t,q,p)$ is jointly $C^2$. Define $\beta=S_\alpha(t,q,\alpha(t,q,p))$; this gives a $C^2$ local map $(q,p)\mapsto(\beta,\alpha)$.

The map $(q,\alpha)\mapsto(\beta=S_\alpha,\alpha)$ has derivative $\begin{pmatrix}S_{\alpha q}&S_{\alpha\alpha}\\0&I\end{pmatrix}$, which is invertible because $S_{\alpha q}=(S_{q\alpha})^T$. By [F1] it has a $C^2$ local inverse solving for $q$ from $(\beta,\alpha)$; then $p=S_q$ gives the $C^2$ inverse map to the one in step 1.1. The equations therefore define the claimed local diffeomorphism.

At fixed $t$, the differential in $(q,\alpha)$ is $d_{(q,\alpha)}S=p_i\,dq^i+\beta^i\,d\alpha_i$. Taking its exterior derivative gives $0=dp_i\wedge dq^i+d\beta^i\wedge d\alpha_i$, hence $\sum_i dq^i\wedge dp_i=\sum_i d\beta^i\wedge d\alpha_i$. This is exactly $F_t^*\omega_{\rm new}=\omega_{\rm old}$ for the source and target forms stated above.

Along a Hamilton characteristic, $\dot q=H_p$ and $\dot p=-H_q$. Differentiate $p=S_q(t,q,\alpha(t,q,p))$ along it, and differentiate the HJ equation in $q$ to obtain $\dot p=-H_q+S_{q\alpha}\dot\alpha$. Since $S_{q\alpha}$ is invertible, $\dot\alpha=0$. Differentiate the HJ equation with respect to $\alpha$: $S_{\alpha t}+S_{\alpha q}H_p=0$. Thus $\dot\beta=\frac d{dt}S_\alpha=S_{\alpha t}+S_{\alpha q}\dot q=0$.

In the temporal chart, $x^0=ct$ implies $p_0=\partial_{x^0}S=S_t/c$. The future mass-shell root [L2] says $p_0=-H/c$, hence $S_t+H(t,q,S_q)=0$. as in [[def-fibre-derivative-and-legendre-transform-of-a-lagrangian]]. In induced coordinates $p_i=\partial L/\partial v^i$.

It is **hyperregular on a declared domain** when $\mathbb F L$ is a diffeomorphism from that entire domain onto an open subset of $\mathbb R\times T^*Q$.

It is **almost regular on a declared domain $\mathcal D_0\subseteq\mathcal D$** when the following are all assumed: $\mathbb F L|_{\mathcal D_0}$ has constant rank; its image $N$ is an embedded submanifold of $\mathbb R\times T^*Q$; its corestriction $\mathcal D_0\to N$ is a surjective submersion (its differential is surjective at every point); and every fibre of that corestriction is connected. These hypotheses are not consequences of singularity alone.

Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$: every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary, of dimension $n$. Its cotangent bundle is

$$T^*Q=\coprod_{q\in Q}T_q^*Q,\qquad \pi:T^*Q\to Q,\quad \pi(q,p)=q,$$

with the canonical smooth structure and induced cotangent charts supplied by the manifold construction in [[def-tautological-one-form-on-a-cotangent-bundle]]. The **tautological one-form** is $\theta_{(q,p)}(\xi)=p(d\pi_{(q,p)}\xi)$, and the **canonical cotangent two-form** is $\omega=-d\theta$. The exact theorem [[thm-the-canonical-cotangent-two-form-is-symplectic]] makes $(T^*Q,\omega)$ a symplectic manifold in the sense of [[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]]. We call this pair the **cotangent phase space** of $Q$.

In an induced chart $(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$, $\theta=p_i\,dq^i$ and $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$. A mathematical **observable** on this phase space means a smooth function $F:T^*Q\to\mathbb R$; this definition does not assert that a measurement has been performed or that every such function is physically measurable.

For an interpreted particle model, assign coordinates $q^i$ their declared units and assign the conjugate covector components $p_i$ units of action divided by the units of $q^i$. Thus $\theta$ and $\omega$ have action units, conventionally joule-seconds, and a bracket of quantities with units \([F]\) and \([G]\) has units \([F][G]/(\text{action})\). These are dimensional interpretations of the model, not additional mathematical premises. The use of $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ is exactly the use in the smooth cotangent-bundle suppliers; no full Axiom of Choice is used.

$$C:=\{z\in U:\chi_1(z)=\cdots=\chi_r(z)=0\}$$

when $d\chi_1(z),\ldots,d\chi_r(z)$ are linearly independent at every $z\in C$. The regular-level theorem [[thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold]] then gives $C$ its embedded-submanifold structure and $T_zC=\bigcap_a\ker d\chi_a(z)$. For functions $F,G$ on $U$, write $F\approx G$ when $F|_C=G|_C$; thus $F\approx0$ means that $F$ vanishes on $C$, without requiring it to vanish off $C$.

Given a smooth canonical Hamiltonian $H_c$ on $U$ and multiplier functions $u^a(t)$, the **total generator** is

$$H_T(t,z):=H_c(t,z)+\sum_{a=1}^r u^a(t)\chi_a(z).$$

The functions $u^a$ are independent parameter functions; the definition does not assert that their equations determine them. If $H_c$ is an energy and $\chi_a$ has units \([\chi_a]\), then $u^a$ has units energy divided by \([\chi_a]\), so every term in $H_T$ has the same units. A later constraint, if generated by consistency, is not declared primary by this definition.

Use the signature $(-,+,+,+)$ throughout. In the flat case, **Minkowski spacetime** means the affine model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]: $A$ is an affine space, $\eta$ is a nondegenerate Lorentz form on its four-dimensional displacement space, and $C^+$ selects the future cone. In the curved case, a **background spacetime** means a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]; the metric and time orientation are fixed data, not dynamical unknowns here. No field equation or completeness assumption is included.

A **massive worldline** on an open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a $C^2$ curve $x:I\to M$ with future-directed timelike tangent $T=dx/ds$ at every parameter value. This is the smooth subclass of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. A **null worldline** is a $C^2$ curve with nonzero future-directed null tangent everywhere. Its tangent has no proper-time normalization: $g(T,T)=0$, so the massive proper-time formula does not apply. In the flat model these are affine curves into $A$ with tangent in the selected future timelike or null cone from [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]].

An **observer at an event** $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Its instantaneous rest space is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$. This is a pointwise vector-space construction; the definition does not assign a clock reading or a moving frame to a lone observer.

An **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth field of future unit timelike vectors on $U$, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]; its observer curves are its integral curves. A **tetrad** is a chosen orthonormal frame field, as in [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. A **chart** is a coordinate map; an adapted chart is a chart whose spatial coordinates are constant along the congruence's integral curves. These objects are distinct: a chart need not be inertial, a tetrad need not be coordinate induced, and a congruence is a field of observers rather than a chart or a frame. This distinction agrees with [[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]].

The coordinates and units used later are SI: in an inertial chart $x^0=ct$ and $x^i$ are metres, $t$ is seconds, $c>0$ is metres per second, and proper time is measured in seconds. In a general chart, coordinate components inherit their coordinate units; invariant equations are tensorial. No global inertial chart, global tetrad, or global observer congruence is asserted to exist.

$$X_H=\frac{\partial H}{\partial p_i}\frac{\partial}{\partial q^i}-\frac{\partial H}{\partial q^i}\frac{\partial}{\partial p_i},\qquad \{F,G\}=F_{q^i}G_{p_i}-F_{p_i}G_{q^i}.$$

If $H_t$ is smooth on an open time-dependent domain $D\subset\mathbb R\times T^*Q$, each solution of $\dot z=X_{H_t}(z)$ has local uniqueness and smooth dependence on initial data and parameters; on its actual interval,

$$\frac{d}{dt}F(t,z(t))=\partial_tF+\{F,H_t\}.$$

No completeness or global flow is asserted. If $H$ is smooth, each local time-$t$ flow map preserves ω.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

For a $C^2$ future-directed timelike worldline $x:I\to M$ on a prescribed smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian background $(M,g,T)$ of signature $(-+++)$, with $m>0$ a fixed primitive mass in kg and $c>0$ in m/s, and any compact segment $[a,b]\subset I$ with $a<b$, adopt the stationary-action model on that segment

$$S_{m,[a,b]}[x]=-mc\int_a^b\sqrt{-g(x',x') }\,d\lambda.$$

Here $x$ is $C^2$ on a neighborhood of $[a,b]$ (so its tangent is $C^1$ there), and $\lambda$ is an increasing regular parameter. An admissible variation is a one-parameter family $x_\epsilon(\lambda)$ that is $C^2$ jointly in $(\epsilon,\lambda)$, has fixed endpoint events $x_\epsilon(a)=x(a)$ and $x_\epsilon(b)=x(b)$, and remains future timelike for sufficiently small $|\epsilon|$. The integrand is the proper-time length density, so $S_{m,[a,b]}=-mc^2\int_a^b d\tau$; its dimension is action (J s). The adopted premise concerns this ideal free test body only. It is neither a theorem about all matter nor an empirical report, and supplies no backreaction or completeness claim. The flat ideal-clock specialization agrees with [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]]; adopting this action on a curved background remains a separate premise.

The cotangent phase-space carrier convention assumes countable choice ACω only; full choice is not assumed.

On a prescribed background $(M,g,T)$, choose an open parameter interval $I$ and a compact segment $[a,b]\subset I$ with $a<b$. In a spacetime chart containing the curve and sufficiently small variations, let $x:I\to M$ be smooth near $[a,b]$, let $p(\lambda)\in T^*_{x(\lambda)}M$ be a smooth covector field along $x$, and let $e$ be smooth and positive near $[a,b]$. Adopt the distinct massless classical particle action on this segment

$$S_{0,[a,b]}[x,p,e]=\int_a^b\left[p_a x'^a-eC_0(x,p)\right]d\lambda,\qquad C_0=\tfrac12g^{ab}p_ap_b.$$

Admissible variations are smooth one-parameter families of chart fields $(x_\epsilon,p_\epsilon,e_\epsilon)$ on a common neighborhood of $[a,b]$, with $x_\epsilon(a)=x(a)$ and $x_\epsilon(b)=x(b)$; the $p_\epsilon$ and $e_\epsilon$ variations are independent and have no endpoint constraints, while $e_\epsilon>0$ for sufficiently small $|\epsilon|$. Impose the physical branch only on stationary solutions after these variations: $p\ne0$ and $p^\sharp$ is future null. With all spacetime coordinates measured in metres and dimensionless $\lambda$, $p_a$ has units kg m/s, $C_0$ has units kg²m²/s² and $e$ has units s/kg, making the action J s. Other parameter units scale $e$ accordingly. This is a separate adopted model: null curves have no proper-time parameter, the model does not arise by setting $m=0$ in $P=mU$, and its positive momentum scale is additional initial data. On the nonzero branch, the vertical differential is $d_pC_0=p^\sharp\ne0$: nondegeneracy of $g^{-1}$ and $p\ne0$ give $p^\sharp\ne0$. Hence the shell is a regular primary constraint in the sense of [[def-rpm-h-regular-constraint-system]]. This postulate is not an empirical observation or a deduction from the massive model.

The cotangent phase-space carrier convention assumes countable choice ACω only; full choice is not assumed.

Let $(M,g,T)$ be a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with signature $(-+++)$. Work in a spacetime chart on a compact parameter interval $[a,b]$ with $a<b$; take $x,p,e$ smooth on a neighbourhood of that interval, $e>0$, $m\ge0$, and $c>0$. Select stationary triples on the future shell branch after taking the independent variations: when $m>0$, $p^\sharp$ is future timelike; when $m=0$, require $p\ne0$ and $p^\sharp$ future null. Set $C_m=\tfrac12(g^{ab}p_ap_b+m^2c^2)$ and define the first-order functional

$$I_m[x,p,e]=\int_a^b\left(p_ax'^a-eC_m(x,p)\right)d\lambda.$$

Take independent smooth variations of $p,e$ and fixed-endpoint variations of $x$. Stationarity on the chart segment is equivalent to

$$x'^a=e g^{ab}p_b,\quad p'_a=-\tfrac e2\partial_a g^{bc}p_bp_c,\quad C_m=0.$$

On the massive future branch $m>0$, these equations are equivalent to stationary paths of the mathematical square-root functional $S[x]=-mc\int_a^b\sqrt{-g(x\prime,x\prime)}\,d\lambda$ on future-timelike curves with fixed endpoints; the fibre-derivative covector is $p=mc\,x'^\flat/\sqrt{-g(x',x')}$, and proper-time gauge has $e=1/m$. For the separate nonzero future-null branch $m=0$, the equations describe a null geodesic with an arbitrary positive parameter multiplier; no proper-time parameter exists. In both cases the unparameterized path is a geodesic, and no existence or completeness claim is made.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $H\in C^\infty(U,\mathbb R)$ on an open set $U\subset\mathbb R\times T^*\mathbb R^n$, with coordinates $(t,q,p)$, and let $S_0\in C^\infty(Q_0,\mathbb R)$ on an open $Q_0\subset\mathbb R^n$. The Hamilton characteristic ODE is $\dot q^i=\partial H/\partial p_i$ and $\dot p_i=-\partial H/\partial q^i$. For a covector $p$ and vector $v$ in the canonical coordinates, write $p\cdot v:=\sum_i p_i v^i$. For each $a_0\in Q_0$ such that $(0,a_0,dS_0(a_0))\in U$, there are neighbourhoods of $(0,a_0)$ and a time interval on which this ODE with $q(0,a)=a$, $p(0,a)=dS_0(a)$ has a smooth solution and $(t,a)\mapsto(t,q(t,a))$ is a diffeomorphism onto its image after restriction. On that image the function

$$S(t,q(t,a))=S_0(a)+\int_0^t[p(u,a)\cdot\dot q(u,a)-H(u,q(u,a),p(u,a))],du$$

is smooth, has initial value $S_0$, and satisfies $S_t+H(t,q,S_q)=0$. The claim is local to the invertible projection domain; it asserts no continuation after a caustic. $S$ has action units, so $[S]=\mathrm{J\,s}$, $[S_q]=[p]$, and $[S_t]=\mathrm J$ when $t,q,p,H$ use SI time, length, momentum, and energy units.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the cotangent/HJ supplier chain and let $n\ge1$. Let $U_H\subset\mathbb R\times T^*\mathbb R^n$ be open and $H\in C^\infty(U_H,\mathbb R)$. Let $D_S\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^n_q\times\mathbb R^n_\alpha$ be open and $S\in C^3(D_S,\mathbb R)$, with $S_t+H(t,q,S_q)=0$ wherever $(t,q,\alpha)\in D_S$ and $(t,q,S_q(t,q,\alpha))\in U_H$. If the mixed matrix $S_{q\alpha}$ is invertible at $(t,q,\alpha)$, then after restricting neighborhoods the equations $p_i=S_{q^i}$, $\beta^i=S_{\alpha_i}$ define a local $C^2$ diffeomorphism $F_t:(q,p)\mapsto(\beta,\alpha)$ at each fixed $t$. Equip the old chart $(q,p)$ with $\omega_{\rm old}=\sum_i dq^i\wedge dp_i$ and the target chart, whose position coordinates are $\beta^i$ and momentum coordinates are $\alpha_i$, with $\omega_{\rm new}=\sum_i d\beta^i\wedge d\alpha_i$. Then $F_t^*\omega_{\rm new}=\omega_{\rm old}$, so this is a local canonical transformation in the stated convention, and $\beta$ is constant along the Hamilton characteristics $\dot q=H_p$, $\dot p=-H_q$. Such a family is a complete integral only on that nonsingular local domain. In the physical interpretation, $q^i,\beta^i$ have units m, $p_i,\alpha_i$ have units kg m/s, $t$ has units s, and $S$ has units J s. In a temporal spacetime chart satisfying H9, the covariant future-shell equation $g^{ab}S_aS_b+m^2c^2=0$ reduces to the time Hamilton–Jacobi equation with $p_0=S_t/c=-H/c$; for $m=0$ require a nonzero future null covector. $S$ is an action, not a dimensionless phase.

For the relativistic shell equation, $m$ is measured in kilograms and $c$ in metres per second.

Let $m\ge0$ and $c>0$. Assume a temporal product chart with lapse-shift data $(N,\beta,h)$ as in [[def-rpm-h-temporal-chart-data]], all four coordinates measured in metres. On the future shell $C_m=\tfrac12(g^{ab}p_ap_b+m^2c^2)=0$, define

$$\kappa=\sqrt{m^2c^2+h^{ij}p_ip_j},\quad p_0=\beta^ip_i-N\kappa,\quad H(t,q,p)=-cp_0=c(N\kappa-\beta^ip_i).$$

For $m=0$, require $p_i\ne0$. Let $J=[t_1,t_2]$ satisfy $t_1<t_2$ and $[ct_1,ct_2]\subset I$, where $I$ is the first-coordinate interval of the temporal product chart; require the path $t\mapsto(ct,q(t))$ to stay in the chart. Take $q^i,p_i$ smooth on a neighborhood of $J$ and vary them by smooth one-parameter families that keep the paths in the chart, fix $q$ at both endpoints and vary $p$ freely; in the massless case the paths and sufficiently small variations stay in $p_i\ne0$. Then the gauge $x^0=ct$ reduces the first-order action to $\int_{t_1}^{t_2}(p_i\dot q^i-H)dt$, and its variational equations on the interior of $J$ are exactly $\dot q^i=H_{p_i}$, $\dot p_i=-H_{q^i}$. The construction is local to this chart and intervals transverse to its time slices; no global curved-space gauge or quotient is asserted.

derivations.claim: Put $p(t)=S_q(t,q(t))$. From $S_t+H(t,q,S_q)=0$, differentiation with respect to $q$ gives $S_{qt}+H_q+H_pS_{qq}=0$. Since $\dot q=H_p$, the chain rule yields $\dot p=S_{qt}+S_{qq}\dot q=-H_q$. Thus $(q,p)$ satisfies both Hamilton equations.

Write $C_m(x,p)=\tfrac12(g^{ab}p_ap_b+m^2c^2)$ and lift the characteristic by $x^0=ct$, $x^i=q^i$, with $p_0=\beta^ip_i-N\kappa$ from [L4]. Set $e:=c/C_{p_0}=cN/\kappa>0$. Implicit differentiation of $C_m(t,q,p_0(t,q,p),p)=0$ gives $H_{p_i}=cC_{p_i}/C_{p_0}=eC_{p_i}$ and $-H_{q^i}=-cC_{q^i}/C_{p_0}=-eC_{q^i}$. Thus $\dot x^0=c=eC_{p_0}$, $\dot x^i=eC_{p_i}$, and $\dot p_i=-eC_{q^i}$. Differentiating $C_m=0$ along the lifted curve makes the $q^i,p_i$ terms cancel and gives $C_{p_0}\dot p_0=-cC_{x^0}$, hence $\dot p_0=-eC_{x^0}$. The lift therefore satisfies the complete H7 first-order shell system. The smooth HJ characteristic and $e$ meet H7's regularity conditions on the compact chart interval.

The inverse projection and complete-integral coordinates from [L2]–[L3] apply only where their Jacobians remain nonsingular. If that projection loses invertibility, the single-valued graph $p=S_q$ used in step 1.1 is no longer supplied; therefore no extension through that point or beyond the actual chart interval follows.

By [A1] or [A2], the massive or separate massless action is adopted on exactly its stated future branch; H7's variational equivalence then identifies the shell trajectory of step 2.1 with a trajectory of that adopted model. This conclusion remains conditional on those physical postulates.

Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$: every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary, of dimension $n$. Its cotangent bundle is

$$T^*Q=\coprod_{q\in Q}T_q^*Q,\qquad \pi:T^*Q\to Q,\quad \pi(q,p)=q,$$

with the canonical smooth structure and induced cotangent charts supplied by the manifold construction in [[def-tautological-one-form-on-a-cotangent-bundle]]. The **tautological one-form** is $\theta_{(q,p)}(\xi)=p(d\pi_{(q,p)}\xi)$, and the **canonical cotangent two-form** is $\omega=-d\theta$. The exact theorem [[thm-the-canonical-cotangent-two-form-is-symplectic]] makes $(T^*Q,\omega)$ a symplectic manifold in the sense of [[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]]. We call this pair the **cotangent phase space** of $Q$.

In an induced chart $(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$, $\theta=p_i\,dq^i$ and $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$. A mathematical **observable** on this phase space means a smooth function $F:T^*Q\to\mathbb R$; this definition does not assert that a measurement has been performed or that every such function is physically measurable.

$$n=N^{-1}(\partial_0-\beta^i\partial_i).$$

Direct contraction gives $g(n,n)=-1$; require that $n$ is future-directed in the supplied time orientation. This field of observers is distinct from the coordinate vector $\partial_0$, which may be spacelike. The coefficients $N,\beta^i,h_{ij}$ are dimensionless when all four coordinates are in metres. In the flat case, **Minkowski spacetime** means the affine model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]: $A$ is an affine space, $\eta$ is a nondegenerate Lorentz form on its four-dimensional displacement space, and $C^+$ selects the future cone. In the curved case, a **background spacetime** means a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]; the metric and time orientation are fixed data, not dynamical unknowns here. No field equation or completeness assumption is included.

A **massive worldline** on an open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a $C^2$ curve $x:I\to M$ with future-directed timelike tangent $T=dx/ds$ at every parameter value. This is the smooth subclass of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. A **null worldline** is a $C^2$ curve with nonzero future-directed null tangent everywhere. Its tangent has no proper-time normalization: $g(T,T)=0$, so the massive proper-time formula does not apply. In the flat model these are affine curves into $A$ with tangent in the selected future timelike or null cone from [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]].

An **observer at an event** $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Its instantaneous rest space is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$. This is a pointwise vector-space construction; the definition does not assign a clock reading or a moving frame to a lone observer.

An **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth field of future unit timelike vectors on $U$, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]; its observer curves are its integral curves. A **tetrad** is a chosen orthonormal frame field, as in [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. A **chart** is a coordinate map; an adapted chart is a chart whose spatial coordinates are constant along the congruence's integral curves. These objects are distinct: a chart need not be inertial, a tetrad need not be coordinate induced, and a congruence is a field of observers rather than a chart or a frame. This distinction agrees with [[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]].

The coordinates and units used later are SI: in an inertial chart $x^0=ct$ and $x^i$ are metres, $t$ is seconds, $c>0$ is metres per second, and proper time is measured in seconds. In a general chart, coordinate components inherit their coordinate units; invariant equations are tensorial. No global inertial chart, global tetrad, or global observer congruence is asserted to exist.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For the group and cotangent conventions of [[def-rpm-h-poincare-charge-space]], the map $\mu:T^*\mathbb R^4\to\mathfrak g^*$ defined by $\langle\mu(x,p),(a,A)\rangle=\ell_{(a,A)}(x,p)$ is a smooth equivariant moment map and obeys

$$\{\ell_\xi,\ell_\eta\}=\ell_{[\xi,\eta]},\quad \{P^a,P^b\}=0,\quad \{J^{ab},P^c\}=\eta^{ac}P^b-\eta^{bc}P^a,$$

$$\{J^{ab},J^{cd}\}=\eta^{ac}J^{bd}-\eta^{ad}J^{bc}-\eta^{bc}J^{ad}+\eta^{bd}J^{ac}.$$

For shell coordinates write $\mathbf p=(p_1,p_2,p_3)$ and $|\mathbf p|^2:=p_1^2+p_2^2+p_3^2$. For each future massive shell with $m>0$ in kg, $c>0$ in m/s, $p_0=-E/c$, and $E=\sqrt{m^2c^4+c^2|\mathbf p|^2}$, or nonzero future null shell with $m=0$ and $|\mathbf p|>0$, its Poincare charges descend to the global ray quotient. For vectors $u,v\in\mathbb R^4$, define $(u\wedge v)^{ab}:=u^av^b-u^bv^a$. The induced dual action is $(P,J)\mapsto(\Lambda P,\Lambda J\Lambda^T+a\wedge\Lambda P)$. On the fixed-time slice $x^0=ct$, with physical position $q^i=x^i$, the boost component $B_i=J^{0i}=ct p_i-q^iE/c$ is explicitly time dependent and satisfies $\partial_tB_i+\{B_i,E\}=0$. These are mathematical identities; conservation is conditional on the stated free-shell evolution.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the referenced cotangent and symplectic-action conventions. Work on affine Minkowski spacetime with inertial coordinates $x^0=ct,x^1,x^2,x^3$ in metres, metric matrix $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and cotangent coordinates $(x^a,p_a)$, where each $p_a$ has SI momentum units. Fix the future cone as the timelike component containing the positive $x^0$ axis, equivalently $v^0>\lvert\mathbf v\rvert$. Let $SO^+(1,3)$ denote the determinant-one, future-cone-preserving Lorentz subgroup. Define the proper orthochronous Poincaré group and its multiplication by

$$G=\mathbb R^4\rtimes SO^+(1,3),\qquad (a,\Lambda)(b,L)=(a+\Lambda b,\Lambda L).$$

Its action on spacetime and the cotangent lift are $x'=\Lambda x+a$ and $p'=\Lambda^{-T}p$. The Lie algebra consists of pairs $(a,A)$ with $A^T\eta+\eta A=0$, bracket

$$[(a,A),(b,B)]=(Ab-Ba,[A,B]).$$

Use the library convention $\xi_M=\left.\frac d{ds}\right|_0\exp_G(-s\xi)\cdot z$. Thus the positive affine generator on spacetime is $Y_{(a,A)}(x)=a+Ax$, the fundamental field is its negative, and the cotangent-lifted positive field is $(a+Ax,-A^Tp)$. Pair the cotangent point with a Lie-algebra element by

$$\ell_{(a,A)}(x,p)=p_b(a^b+A^b{}_cx^c).$$

Define $P^a=\eta^{ab}p_b$ and $J^{ab}=x^aP^b-x^bP^a$. The equivalent dual pairing is $\ell_{(a,A)}=p_ba^b-\tfrac12J_{bc}A^{bc}$, where $A^{bc}=A^b{}_d\eta^{dc}$ and $J_{bc}=\eta_{bd}\eta_{ce}J^{de}$. Here $[P^a]=\mathrm{kg\,m/s}$ and $[J^{ab}]=\mathrm{J\,s}$. These are charge-space definitions on the full cotangent bundle; shell reduction and the moment-map identities are stated separately. No spin or particle model is included.

derivations.claim: By the canonical product bracket, $\{q_aE_a,p_1+p_2\}=E_a$ for each $a$, since $E_a$ is independent of position; also $\{t(p_1+p_2),p_1+p_2\}=0$. Hence $\{K,P\}=(E_1+E_2)/c^2$.

The Hamiltonian is $H=E_1+E_2+kr^2/2$, so $H/c^2-\{K,P\}=kr^2/(2c^2)>0$ whenever $r=q_1-q_2\ne0$. The required algebra relation in [L1] fails there. Since $k$ has units $\mathrm{kg/s^2}$, $kr^2/2$ is energy and the compared charges have matching units. This refutes this proposed free-boost construction only.

Assume countable choice ACω, as in [[def-countable-choice]], for the smooth cotangent-bundle carrier convention used by this page; no full Axiom of Choice is assumed.

Fix a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,T)$ with signature $(-+++)$, as in [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. Here $T$ denotes the supplied smooth timelike field selecting the future cone, called $N$ in that geometric definition. Use the distinction among a spacetime, a worldline, a pointwise observer, an observer congruence, a tetrad and a chart given in [[def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline]]. This definition does not make $g$ dynamical.

In this relativistic-particle model, $m>0$ is a fixed **primitive mass parameter** measured in kilograms, and $c>0$ is a fixed **primitive conversion parameter** measured in metres per second. They are parameters of the adopted physical formulation, not quantities derived by this definition. Coordinates $x^a$ in an SI chart have length units; a cotangent vector $p=p_a\,dx^a$ has units of momentum, $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, when all four coordinates are in metres. The canonical one-form $p_a\,dx^a$ therefore has action units $\mathrm{J\,s}$. Along a future-directed timelike curve with tangent $V=dx/d\lambda$, set $s:=\sqrt{-g(V,V)}$; then $d\tau=s\,d\lambda/c$, independently of the increasing regular parameter. The length action $-mc\int s\,d\lambda$ has action units. For a future unit observer $n$ and future causal covector $p$, define the model normal-observer energy and spatial momentum covector by

$$E_n(p):=-c\,p(n),\qquad q_n(p):=p+p(n)n^\flat,$$

where $n^\flat=g(n,\cdot)$. The restriction of $g^{-1}$ to covectors annihilating $n$ is positive definite, so it supplies the norm of $q_n(p)$. These are quantity definitions and unit conventions; they do not identify canonical momentum with mechanical momentum, assert that an apparatus measured these values, or establish a dynamical law.

unresolved_inputs.actual_statement_excerpt:
Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$: every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary, of dimension $n$. Its cotangent bundle is

$$T^*Q=\coprod_{q\in Q}T_q^*Q,\qquad \pi:T^*Q\to Q,\quad \pi(q,p)=q,$$

with the canonical smooth structure and induced cotangent charts supplied by the manifold construction in [[def-tautological-one-form-on-a-cotangent-bundle]]. The **tautological one-form** is $\theta_{(q,p)}(\xi)=p(d\pi_{(q,p)}\xi)$, and the **canonical cotangent two-form** is $\omega=-d\theta$. The exact theorem [[thm-the-canonical-cotangent-two-form-is-symplectic]] makes $(T^*Q,\omega)$ a symplectic manifold in the sense of [[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]]. We call this pair the **cotangent phase space** of $Q$.

In an induced chart $(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$, $\theta=p_i\,dq^i$ and $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$. A mathematical **observable** on this phase space means a smooth function $F:T^*Q\to\mathbb R$; this definition does not assert that a measurement has been performed or that every such function is physically measurable.

For an interpreted particle model, assign coordinates $q^i$ their declared units and assign the conjugate covector components $p_i$ units of action divided by the units of $q^i$. Thus $\theta$ and $\omega$ have action units, conventionally joule-seconds, and a bracket of quantities with units \([F]\) and \([G]\) has units \([F][G]/(\text{action})\). These are dimensional interpretations of the model, not additional mathematical premises. The use of $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ is exactly the use in the smooth cotangent-bundle suppliers; no full Axiom of Choice is used.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ and let $(M^{2n},\omega)$ be a smooth symplectic manifold. A finite family of smooth functions $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_r$ defined on an open neighborhood $U\subseteq M$ is a **regular primary constraint family** on

$$C:=\{z\in U:\chi_1(z)=\cdots=\chi_r(z)=0\}$$

when $d\chi_1(z),\ldots,d\chi_r(z)$ are linearly independent at every $z\in C$. The regular-level theorem [[thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold]] then gives $C$ its embedded-submanifold structure and $T_zC=\bigcap_a\ker d\chi_a(z)$. For functions $F,G$ on $U$, write $F\approx G$ when $F|_C=G|_C$; thus $F\approx0$ means that $F$ vanishes on $C$, without requiring it to vanish off $C$.

Given a smooth canonical Hamiltonian $H_c$ on $U$ and multiplier functions $u^a(t)$, the **total generator** is

$$H_T(t,z):=H_c(t,z)+\sum_{a=1}^r u^a(t)\chi_a(z).$$

The functions $u^a$ are independent parameter functions; the definition does not assert that their equations determine them. If $H_c$ is an energy and $\chi_a$ has units \([\chi_a]\), then $u^a$ has units energy divided by \([\chi_a]\), so every term in $H_T$ has the same units. A later constraint, if generated by consistency, is not declared primary by this definition.

unresolved_inputs.actual_statement_excerpt:
Use the signature $(-,+,+,+)$ throughout. In the flat case, **Minkowski spacetime** means the affine model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]: $A$ is an affine space, $\eta$ is a nondegenerate Lorentz form on its four-dimensional displacement space, and $C^+$ selects the future cone. In the curved case, a **background spacetime** means a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]; the metric and time orientation are fixed data, not dynamical unknowns here. No field equation or completeness assumption is included.

A **massive worldline** on an open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a $C^2$ curve $x:I\to M$ with future-directed timelike tangent $T=dx/ds$ at every parameter value. This is the smooth subclass of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. A **null worldline** is a $C^2$ curve with nonzero future-directed null tangent everywhere. Its tangent has no proper-time normalization: $g(T,T)=0$, so the massive proper-time formula does not apply. In the flat model these are affine curves into $A$ with tangent in the selected future timelike or null cone from [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]].

An **observer at an event** $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Its instantaneous rest space is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$. This is a pointwise vector-space construction; the definition does not assign a clock reading or a moving frame to a lone observer.

An **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth field of future unit timelike vectors on $U$, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]; its observer curves are its integral curves. A **tetrad** is a chosen orthonormal frame field, as in [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. A **chart** is a coordinate map; an adapted chart is a chart whose spatial coordinates are constant along the congruence's integral curves. These objects are distinct: a chart need not be inertial, a tetrad need not be coordinate induced, and a congruence is a field of observers rather than a chart or a frame. This distinction agrees with [[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]].

The coordinates and units used later are SI: in an inertial chart $x^0=ct$ and $x^i$ are metres, $t$ is seconds, $c>0$ is metres per second, and proper time is measured in seconds. In a general chart, coordinate components inherit their coordinate units; invariant equations are tensorial. No global inertial chart, global tetrad, or global observer congruence is asserted to exist.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $(P,\omega)$ be a smooth symplectic manifold with its induced Poisson bracket, and let $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_r$ be a regular constraint family on a common zero surface $N=\{z:\chi_a(z)=0\}$ as defined by [[def-rpm-h-regular-constraint-system]]. The family is **first-class on $N$** when

$$\{\chi_a,\chi_b\}(z)=0\qquad\text{for every }z\in N\text{ and all }a,b.$$

Equivalently, each pairwise bracket is weakly zero in the notation $F\approx0$ of [[def-rpm-h-regular-constraint-system]]. The Poisson bracket convention is that of [[thm-rpm-h-canonical-poisson-and-flow]]. This definition is a pointwise closure condition on the stated regular surface; it does not assert multiplier-algorithm termination or global quotient regularity.

Let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional smooth manifold as in [[def-rpm-h-cotangent-phase-space]], and write its cotangent phase space in induced coordinates $(q^i,p_i)$. With $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$, define $X_H$ by $\iota_{X_H}\omega=dH$ and define the Poisson bracket by $\{F,G\}:=X_G(F)$. Then

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the cotangent/HJ supplier chain and let $n\ge1$. Let $U_H\subset\mathbb R\times T^*\mathbb R^n$ be open and $H\in C^\infty(U_H,\mathbb R)$. Let $D_S\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^n_q\times\mathbb R^n_\alpha$ be open and $S\in C^3(D_S,\mathbb R)$, with $S_t+H(t,q,S_q)=0$ wherever $(t,q,\alpha)\in D_S$ and $(t,q,S_q(t,q,\alpha))\in U_H$. If the mixed matrix $S_{q\alpha}$ is invertible at $(t,q,\alpha)$, then after restricting neighborhoods the equations $p_i=S_{q^i}$, $\beta^i=S_{\alpha_i}$ define a local $C^2$ diffeomorphism $F_t:(q,p)\mapsto(\beta,\alpha)$ at each fixed $t$. Equip the old chart $(q,p)$ with $\omega_{\rm old}=\sum_i dq^i\wedge dp_i$ and the target chart, whose position coordinates are $\beta^i$ and momentum coordinates are $\alpha_i$, with $\omega_{\rm new}=\sum_i d\beta^i\wedge d\alpha_i$. Then $F_t^*\omega_{\rm new}=\omega_{\rm old}$, so this is a local canonical transformation in the stated convention, and $\beta$ is constant along the Hamilton characteristics $\dot q=H_p$, $\dot p=-H_q$. Such a family is a complete integral only on that nonsingular local domain. In the physical interpretation, $q^i,\beta^i$ have units m, $p_i,\alpha_i$ have units kg m/s, $t$ has units s, and $S$ has units J s. In a temporal spacetime chart satisfying H9, the covariant future-shell equation $g^{ab}S_aS_b+m^2c^2=0$ reduces to the time Hamilton–Jacobi equation with $p_0=S_t/c=-H/c$; for $m=0$ require a nonzero future null covector. $S$ is an action, not a dimensionless phase.

For the relativistic shell equation, $m$ is measured in kilograms and $c$ in metres per second.

In affine Minkowski space with $x^0=ct$, let $m\ge0$, $p_i$ be spatial momentum components and $p_i\ne0$ for $m=0$. On the future shell, $p_0=-E/c$, where

$$E(\mathbf p)=\sqrt{m^2c^4+c^2|\mathbf p|^2}.$$

On any compact interval $J=[t_1,t_2]$ of inertial time with $t_1<t_2$, the gauge $x^0=ct$ reduces the first-order shell action to

$$I_J=\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\left(p_i\dot q^i-E(\mathbf p)\right)dt,\qquad q^i=x^i.$$

For this variational statement, take $q^i$ and $p_i$ smooth on a neighborhood of $J$ and restrict to variations that are smooth one-parameter families, fix $q$ at both endpoints, and vary $p$ freely; in the massless case the paths and sufficiently small variations stay in $\mathbf p\ne0$. The resulting Hamilton equations hold on the interior of $J$.

The gauge pair $C_m=0$, $\psi=x^0-ct=0$ is second class because $\{C_m,\psi\}=-P^0\ne0$ on the future shell; its Dirac reduction gives the canonical spatial bracket. The reduced Hamilton equations are $\dot q^i=c^2p_i/E$, $\dot p_i=0$, agreeing with the unreduced characteristic trajectories. On this full flat future shell every characteristic line meets each inertial-time slice once; this global assertion does not extend by this proof to a curved temporal chart.

derivations.claim: Differentiation gives $S_q=\alpha$, $S_t=-E(\alpha)$, and hence $S_t+E(S_q)=0$. Also $S_{q_i\alpha_j}=\delta_{ij}$, so its determinant is one. By [L1] this nonsingular family supplies local canonical integration coordinates on the stated domain.

Differentiating $E$ gives $\partial_{\alpha_i}E=c^2\alpha_i/E$ wherever $E>0$. Thus $\beta=S_\alpha=q-tc^2\alpha/E$ and rearranging yields the stated trajectory formula. For $m=0$, $E=c|\alpha|>0$ and differentiability requires $\alpha\ne0$, which is exactly the given domain.

The products $q\cdot\alpha$ and $tE$ have action units, while $\alpha$ is momentum and $\partial_\alpha S$ is length. Hence the generating function and canonical coordinates have the claimed physical dimensions.

Let $\mathcal D$ be an open subset of the time-dependent tangent bundle $\mathbb R\times TQ$ of a finite-dimensional smooth manifold $Q$, and let $L:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R$ be smooth. For fixed $t$, the **fibre derivative** is the map

$$\mathbb F L(t,q,v)=(t,q,p),\qquad p(w)=\left.\frac{d}{ds}\right|_{s=0}L(t,q,v+sw),$$

as in [[def-fibre-derivative-and-legendre-transform-of-a-lagrangian]]. In induced coordinates $p_i=\partial L/\partial v^i$.

The Lagrangian is **regular** at $(t,q,v)$ when the velocity Hessian $(\partial^2L/\partial v^i\partial v^j)$ is invertible there; regularity gives only a local inverse branch. It is **hyperregular on a declared domain** when $\mathbb F L$ is a diffeomorphism from that entire domain onto an open subset of $\mathbb R\times T^*Q$.

It is **almost regular on a declared domain $\mathcal D_0\subseteq\mathcal D$** when the following are all assumed: $\mathbb F L|_{\mathcal D_0}$ has constant rank; its image $N$ is an embedded submanifold of $\mathbb R\times T^*Q$; its corestriction $\mathcal D_0\to N$ is a surjective submersion (its differential is surjective at every point); and every fibre of that corestriction is connected. These hypotheses are not consequences of singularity alone.

$$E_n(p):=-c\,p(n),\qquad q_n(p):=p+p(n)n^\flat,$$

where $n^\flat=g(n,\cdot)$. The restriction of $g^{-1}$ to covectors annihilating $n$ is positive definite, so it supplies the norm of $q_n(p)$. Given a smooth canonical Hamiltonian $H_c$ on $U$ and multiplier functions $u^a(t)$, the **total generator** is

$$H_T(t,z):=H_c(t,z)+\sum_{a=1}^r u^a(t)\chi_a(z).$$

The functions $u^a$ are independent parameter functions; the definition does not assert that their equations determine them. If $H_c$ is an energy and $\chi_a$ has units \([\chi_a]\), then $u^a$ has units energy divided by \([\chi_a]\), so every term in $H_T$ has the same units. A later constraint, if generated by consistency, is not declared primary by this definition.

Let $(M,g,T)$ be a smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-+++)$, with the geometric meaning fixed by [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. Here $T$ denotes the future-cone field called $N$ in that definition. A **temporal product chart** is a smooth coordinate map from an open product $I\times\Omega\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3$ onto an open subset of $M$, with coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$. We require $x^0$ to have length units and each $x^i$ to have length units in the physical interpretation.

$$g=-N^2(dx^0)^2+h_{ij}(dx^i+\beta^i dx^0)(dx^j+\beta^j dx^0).$$

Write $h^{ij}$ for the inverse matrix. The normal field is

$$n=N^{-1}(\partial_0-\beta^i\partial_i).$$

Direct contraction gives $g(n,n)=-1$; require that $n$ is future-directed in the supplied time orientation. This field of observers is distinct from the coordinate vector $\partial_0$, which may be spacelike. The coefficients $N,\beta^i,h_{ij}$ are dimensionless when all four coordinates are in metres. This definition is local to the specified product chart; it asserts no global temporal foliation.

Use the signature $(-,+,+,+)$ throughout. In the flat case, **Minkowski spacetime** means the affine model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]: $A$ is an affine space, $\eta$ is a nondegenerate Lorentz form on its four-dimensional displacement space, and $C^+$ selects the future cone. In the curved case, a **background spacetime** means a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]; the metric and time orientation are fixed data, not dynamical unknowns here. No field equation or completeness assumption is included.

A **massive worldline** on an open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a $C^2$ curve $x:I\to M$ with future-directed timelike tangent $T=dx/ds$ at every parameter value. This is the smooth subclass of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. A **null worldline** is a $C^2$ curve with nonzero future-directed null tangent everywhere. Its tangent has no proper-time normalization: $g(T,T)=0$, so the massive proper-time formula does not apply. In the flat model these are affine curves into $A$ with tangent in the selected future timelike or null cone from [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]].

An **observer at an event** $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Its instantaneous rest space is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$. This is a pointwise vector-space construction; the definition does not assign a clock reading or a moving frame to a lone observer.

An **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth field of future unit timelike vectors on $U$, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]; its observer curves are its integral curves. A **tetrad** is a chosen orthonormal frame field, as in [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. A **chart** is a coordinate map; an adapted chart is a chart whose spatial coordinates are constant along the congruence's integral curves. These objects are distinct: a chart need not be inertial, a tetrad need not be coordinate induced, and a congruence is a field of observers rather than a chart or a frame. This distinction agrees with [[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]].

The coordinates and units used later are SI: in an inertial chart $x^0=ct$ and $x^i$ are metres, $t$ is seconds, $c>0$ is metres per second, and proper time is measured in seconds. In a general chart, coordinate components inherit their coordinate units; invariant equations are tensorial. No global inertial chart, global tetrad, or global observer congruence is asserted to exist.
